title: T1496.002 — Resource Hijacking - Bandwidth Hijacking
subtitle: This simulation shows how an ordinary home laptop becomes a criminal proxy node - and how the SOC (security operations center - the team that watches security alerts) finds it.

nodes.label: Sensitive data
nodes.tip: Sensitive data - What is at risk

steps.title: The tempting download
steps.caption: A user downloads a cracked game or a "free" VPN app from a file-sharing site. The attacker packed a pay-per-install bundle into it. Nothing is flagged yet, because pirated downloads are common and mostly invisible to security tools
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Silent proxy install
steps.caption: While the game installs, the bundle drops a proxy client and registers it as a service. The user sees only the game. On a monitored device, Sysmon (a Windows tool that records process and network events) would record the client starting from a Temp folder with a name that imitates the Windows file svchost.exe - for example svhost.exe
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Joining the proxy pool
steps.caption: The client connects to the proxy network and registers the laptop as an exit node. It holds one connection open for many hours and uploads steadily. Zeek or NetFlow later shows a session of about 14 hours with 6 GB of upload - far beyond any normal app on that device
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Fraud through the victim IP
steps.caption: A criminal rents the laptop's IP address and routes bank fraud through it. To the bank, the criminal appears to connect from the victim's home address. Nothing on the laptop changes; the first evidence is external
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Abuse reports arrive
steps.caption: Fraud victims, banks, and fraud-detection teams complain. The ISP abuse desk receives reports about the IP, and the address lands on a blocklist. For many organizations this is the very first signal - external, not internal

steps.title: The SOC joins the signals
steps.caption: The SOC correlates three weak signals into one incident: an unknown service on the laptop, a 14-hour upload-heavy session, and an abuse report for the same host. Each alone is noise; together they are proof
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Remove, block, report
steps.caption: The SOC quarantines the laptop, deletes the proxy service and its persistence, and blocks proxy egress at the firewall. The long session ends, and abuse reports stop within days
steps.defender: Edge, DNS and network-flow telemetry provide the first reliable evidence.

steps.title: Prevent the next one
steps.caption: The team bans pirated software, builds upload baselines per host class, blocks proxy and tracker egress, and starts weekly IP reputation checks. The entry and the monetization are both closed
